name: Markdown
description: Reading a specification written as Markdown into the shape every mechanism judges against.

text: A specification written this way is the document a person reads as well as
the reference line the tool compares against, so what the reading recovers
is the structure a reader already sees: a title, the globs a Scope section
lists, a scenario heading opening with its id, and the rows stating its steps.
The grammar refuses nothing — every byte sequence is a legal document — so
every shape rule below is the reading's own, and each answers at the line
that broke it rather than at the file.
What names a grammar asks for those blocks and nothing else; what decides
the meaning of them names none. That is why the scenarios about meaning are
claimed from a test whose snapshot can still be regenerated.

scenarios.title: A document read into a feature and its scenarios
given: a document with a title, a Scope section and one scenario
scenarios.when: the blocks the document is made of are read
scenarios.then: the feature carries the title, the globs it scopes by, and the scenario with its steps

scenarios.title: A paragraph wrapped for a reader says what an unwrapped one says
given: a description written across several lines
scenarios.when: the blocks the document is made of are read
scenarios.then: each soft line break answers as a single space

scenarios.title: A scenario standing on two states
given: a scenario stating Given twice and no Then
scenarios.when: the blocks the document is made of are read
scenarios.then: both states are held under given, and no then is held at all

scenarios.title: An id with nothing written after it
given: a scenario heading that is an id and nothing else
scenarios.when: the blocks the document is made of are read
scenarios.then: the scenario carries the id and no title

scenarios.title: Prose written under a scenario is prose
given: a paragraph under the title and another under a scenario
scenarios.when: the blocks the document is made of are read
scenarios.then: the feature says what the paragraph under the title says

scenarios.title: A scenario heading naming no id
given: a scenario heading that does not open with a code span
scenarios.when: the blocks the document is made of are read
scenarios.then: the specification is refused, answering at that heading

scenarios.title: A pair of backticks with nothing between them
given: a scenario heading opening with an empty code span
scenarios.when: the blocks the document is made of are read
scenarios.then: the specification is refused, answering at that heading

scenarios.title: An include that is not taken letter for letter
given: a Scope section listing a glob outside backticks
scenarios.when: the blocks the document is made of are read
scenarios.then: the specification is refused, answering at that item

scenarios.title: A step row that lost a separator
given: a step row the grammar reads as one cell
scenarios.when: the blocks the document is made of are read
scenarios.then: the specification is refused, answering at that row

scenarios.title: A step row carrying a separator nobody escaped
given: a step row the grammar reads as three cells
scenarios.when: the blocks the document is made of are read
scenarios.then: the specification is refused, answering at that row

scenarios.title: A row naming something that is not a step
given: a step row whose first cell is neither Given, When nor Then
scenarios.when: the blocks the document is made of are read
scenarios.then: the specification is refused, naming the word it was given

scenarios.title: A step with no scenario to belong to
given: a step row written before any scenario heading
scenarios.when: the blocks the document is made of are read
scenarios.then: the specification is refused, answering at that row

scenarios.title: A document that names nothing
scenarios.when: the blocks the document is made of are read
scenarios.then: the specification is refused, since nothing says what it answers for

scenarios.title: A document that names itself twice
scenarios.when: the blocks the document is made of are read
scenarios.then: the specification is refused, answering at the second one

scenarios.title: A real document read through the grammar
given: a specification file written as Markdown
scenarios.when: the reading is asked what it declares
scenarios.then: the blocks the query asks for answer with the lines they sit on

scenarios.title: Which reading answers for a file
scenarios.when: the reading is asked whether it reads it
scenarios.then: only a path ending in the extension it is written for answers yes

scenarios.title: The same specification written both ways
given: one specification written as Markdown and as JSON
scenarios.when: each is read by the reading answering for it
scenarios.then: the two answer alike in every field but the path and the line
